study: Konstantopoulos, Miller & van der Ploeg 2013 (EEPA) — Indiana mCLASS/Acuity interim-assessment RCT
eval_evidence: Impact evaluation conducted by IES-funded academic researchers (Konstantopoulos et al., grant R305E090005); the program was Indiana DOE's statewide interim-assessment rollout using commercial vendor products (Wireless Generation mCLASS, CTB/McGraw-Hill Acuity). Evaluators had no developer stake.
developer_evidence: PD was delivered as part of Indiana's statewide system rollout — 'Indiana began the roll-out of the assessment program in summer 2008 by training' users, and the vendors provided 'training associated with each product.' The impact-evaluation research team did not deliver the PD; the state/vendor system did.
cascade_evidence: The papers say the state/vendors trained users in the statewide rollout but do not specify whether trainers reached classroom teachers directly or via a district/lead-trainer cascade. Publication silent on transmission hops.
counterfactual_evidence: Control schools 'did not receive any treatment' / 'did not receive access to these assessments and their associated trainings, and operated under business-as-usual conditions.' True BAU.
coaching_evidence: Intervention = interim-assessment system plus vendor training on using the diagnostic data; the publication does not describe the PD format/intensity or any ongoing in-class coaching component (no coaching mentioned, but format not detailed).
student_dose_evidence: Students take the interim/diagnostic assessments directly (mCLASS face-to-face probes; Acuity online tests during class periods), but these are diagnostic assessments informing the teacher's regular instruction, not an added tutoring/pull-out/extra-instruction dose.
maturity_evidence: RCT treatment year was 2009-2010, the first implementation year for the volunteer schools (volunteered spring 2009); the paper repeatedly frames 'the first year of the experiment.' Outcomes measured at end of that year. (Companion 2016 paper notes ~10 schools had some prior vendor exposure.)
